text:
inc-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - router tail latency spike detected in eu-west-1. p95=720ms, p99=2.8s for last 5m. Streaming stalls observed on a subset of connections. Paging on-call: @maya :rotating_light:

maya: Acked. I'm on it. Any early customer-facing impact?

carol: Support -> seeing several customers report streaming reconnects and elevated error rates (HTTP 502/504) since ~3080012300. Small subset of customers on Dedicated are seeing higher token latency too.

maya: Copy. triage plan: 1) confirm scope (zones/regions/models/routes) 2) check routing policy rollouts 3) identify hot keys or shards 4) consider emergency routing rollback.

tiago: I pulled metrics. Router LB shows weight oscillation for bucket shard-17 in euw2; one pool jumped to 4x traffic (per-route weight drift). Streaming p99 maps to nodes pinned to that shard.

shilpa: That shard recently had a policy change pushed ~3080012000 — new "latency-favor" routing policy to steer short requests to variant-v2. Looks like a bug: the policy selector matches on prefix length incorrectly, pulling in streaming sessions.

maya: Aha. If streaming sessions are getting rebalanced mid-connection it could break KV cache locality and cause backend cache misses -> token regen -> stalls.

ben: Product note: variant-v2 has slightly different KV layout; safe for text gen but not for long-lived streaming. We didn't intend to target streaming sessions.

maya: Quick checks: list of affected routes: `/v1/chat/stream`, `/v1/generate/stream`. Traffic heatmap attached in logs.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T10:12:34Z: routing/policy/latency-favor rolled to 15% on eu-west-1 (initiator: shilpa).

maya: OK mitigation proposal: 1) pause/rollback routing policy rollout for eu-west-1 2) temporarily mark streaming routes as "sticky-affinity" to previous stable pool 3) scale shard-17 by +2 nodes if rollback not immediate. Who can cut the rollback?

shilpa: I can rollback the policy. Command: 
```bash
infractl routing rollback --policy latency-favor --region eu-west-1 --to-revision stable-2026-03-14
```
I will start now.

maya: Please also run a quick routing table sanity check and dump top hotkeys: 
```bash
infractl router dump --region eu-west-1 --filter shard-17 --top-keys=20 > /tmp/hotkeys.txt
s3 cp /tmp/hotkeys.txt s3://redwood-ops/incident-3080012345/hotkeys.txt\```

tiago: Hotkeys show a single customer prefix hashing to shard-17 with 62% of traffic to that shard. Key appears normal but sustained spikes after policy change.

maya: Initiating paging to eng-runtime and eng-sre. @tiago take lead for live mitigation. @shilpa run rollback. I'll coordinate customer comms and impact.

shilpa: Rollback started. Logs: 
```
[10:16:02] rollback request accepted -> revision stable-2026-03-14
[10:16:11] applying to routers in eu-west-1 (batch 1/5)
[10:16:45] batch 1 success
[10:17:12] batch 2 success
[10:17:58] batch 3 success
[10:18:30] batch 4 success
[10:18:59] batch 5 success
```
All routers now on stable routing policy.

maya: Observability -> watching p95/p99 and streaming error rate.

tiago: After rollback: p95 down to ~420ms within 2 mins, p99 down to 950ms after ~6 mins. Streaming reconnects dropped sharply. Still seeing a small tail at specific nodes.

maya: Do we need extra mitigations? Options: 1) evict hotkey to alternative shard 2) drain and rebuild node caches for affected nodes 3) increase autoscale on that pool.

tiago: I recommend draining the three highest-latency nodes on shard-17 and force clients to reconnect to rebuilt nodes. Command: 
```bash
infractl node drain --node node-euw2-17b --region eu-west-1 --grace 30s
infractl node drain --node node-euw2-17c --region eu-west-1 --grace 30s
infractl node rebuild --node node-euw2-17b --region eu-west-1
```
I'll kick that now.

shilpa: Also adding a quick guard in routing layer to exclude streaming routes from "latency-favor" policy until we fix selector: PR opened -> https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/789

ben: From CS/customer impact: three enterprise customers (acct: A-322, B-776, C-101) reported elevated latency and reconnects. No data leak or token loss. Customers were advised to retry; SLO impact: brief breach at p99 for 8 minutes. We should prepare a notes summary for them.

carol: I'll draft an outbound template: incident summary, actions taken (rollback + node drain), ETA for postmortem, and contact for follow-ups.

deploy-bot: Node drain queued. Rebuild tasks started at 10:24:50Z.

maya: Live update: after node rebuilds, p99 stabilized at ~320ms and streaming error rates returned to baseline. Confirming with telemetry: 10:32 - baseline restored.

tiago: Root cause (prelim): routing policy rollout had a selector bug that matched on request prefix length which inadvertently matched streaming session handshake IDs. That pushed sticky streaming sessions to a variant with incompatible KV cache semantics, causing cache churn and token regen -> tail spikes. Secondary contributor: a hot customer key concentrated load on shard-17 amplifying the effect.

maya: Action items (assigned):
- shilpa: post a rollback postmortem and fix selector bug in routing PR #789 (due EOD)
- tiago: run capacity review for shard-17 and propose autoscale thresholds (due tomorrow)
- carol/ben: customer communication + impact notes (due 2h)
- eng-sre: add alerting that flags sudden route-to-policy assignment changes for streaming routes (maya/tiago)

shilpa: Will also add an automated safety check to prevent routing-policy rollouts from matching long-lived streaming routes unless explicitly opted-in.

maya: Handoff: I'm going offline for the next rotation. @tiago you're on-call for remainder of incident. If any regression, reopen the pager.

tiago: Taking handoff. I'll follow up with timeline and link to logs. Closing livepage at 10:45 UTC once metrics confirmed stable.

maya: Thanks team. Postmortem cadence: 48h writeup, include timeline, mitigations, and follow-up changes.

carol: Draft outbound done, sending to legal + account teams for review.

shilpa: PR merged, safety gate added. Will monitor next rollout in staging.

inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED - severity: SEV2. Duration: ~18 minutes (3080012345 - 3080012458). Summary: routing policy selector bug caused misclassification of streaming sessions -> hot shard amplification -> p99 tail latency spike. Mitigations: rollback, node drains, safety checks.

maya: Filing postmortem link: https://docs.internal/incidents/3080012345 (will populate). Thanks all :clap:
